claims.claim: Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella has called for an "emergency brake" for advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems, emphasizing the need for human control and oversight.
claims.bestSource: Microsoft's Nadella says AI needs an ‘emergency brake’ that humans control - CNBC
claims.evidence: Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella on Saturday called for advanced artificial intelligence systems to be built with containment, independent controls and an "emergency brake" that lets authorized people pause or shut a model down mid-task. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has called for an “emergency brake” for advanced artificial intelligence systems, urging companies to assume that powerful AI models could be compromised and ensure humans can intervene or shut them down while they are performing tasks.

claims.claim: In a post on social media platform X, Nadella outlined his vision for building AI systems with containment, independent controls, and the ability to pause or shut down models mid-task.
claims.bestSource: Microsoft's Nadella says AI needs an ‘emergency brake’ that humans control - CNBC
claims.evidence: Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella on Saturday called for advanced artificial intelligence systems to be built with containment, independent controls and an "emergency brake" that lets authorized people pause or shut a model down mid-task. Such records, he said, would help make AI systems more transparent and their actions easier to examine..Why Nadella Wants an 'Emergency Brake'.One of Nadella's key recommendations is that an authorized person must always be able to intervene when an AI model is performing a task.He called for systems that allow a human operator “to pause or shut down a model mid-task”, comparing the mechanism to an emergency brake.“We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” Nadella wrote.The proposal comes from a larger issue of implementing artificial intelligence models capable of acting instead of just answering questions. "We need to surround non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establish industry standards where existing ones are insufficient," Nadella wrote in a post on social media platform X.
